product: Crude oil, approximately 100% oil, from the Santa Ynez Unit (Platforms Harmony, Heritage, Hondo) offshore California, transported through Santa Ynez Pipeline System segments CA-324 and CA-325.
demand: California refinery demand. Barrels cleared in Q2 2026 only because refiners displaced imported cargos, and offtake is limited by refinery willingness and sulfur specifications rather than by global oil demand.
pricing_power: Weak. Sable is a Brent-linked price taker on a newly restarted Pacific OCS stream facing sulfur quality deducts and $24-28 per Bbl marketing and GP and T deducts, with $65 Brent collars as floor protection.
competition: Competes with imported crude cargos and other California producers for scarce refinery slots; no pricing moat. California regulatory and political opposition is the binding rivalry.
team: Chairman and CEO Jim Flores; investor contact Harrison Breaud, VP Finance and Investor Relations. The company describes its team as having extensive California operating experience.
market_strategy: Ramp SYU production and pipeline throughput, cut 2H26 capex 41% to $85M midpoint, amortize the TLB via 100% quarterly excess-cash-flow sweep, hedge Brent collars, and evaluate the $125M Buoy and $475M OS&T vessel options plus waterborne marketing for alternative market access.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue $137.1M, net sales ~21 Mbbl/d rising to ~40 Mbo/d on exit; refinancing closed 2026-07-02 extended maturities, repaid Exxon, and 2026-08-19 order avoided an injunction; Roth MKM raised PT to $11 on 2026-08-26.
bear: 2026-08-19 court found consent-decree violation without justification, rejected force majeure and DPA immunity, $1.449M penalty; 40 Mbo/d throughput cap, sulfur deducts, $18.5M demurrage, 15% coupon with 100% cash sweep, Jefferies cut PT to $9 on 2026-08-12.
falsifier: Platform Hondo fails to restart by 2026-09-30, or Q3 2026 net sales come in below 40,000 Boe/d, showing the ramp and throughput cap bind.
web_what_changed: 2026-07-02 refinancing closed: $675M TLB at 15% coupon due Dec 15 2028, $345M 6.5% converts at $4.00, $115M equity at $3.08, Exxon term loan repaid, maturity extended. 2026-08-10 Q2 2026: $137.1M revenue, 21 net Mbbl/d, ~40 Mbo/d exit. 2026-08-19/24 court order modified consent decree to PHMSA, $1.449M penalty, no injunction.
web_not_known_yesterday: not found - no company press release, wire or filing since the 2026-08-24 8-K court-order filing; last trade 2026-09-24 closed $3.97 with $4.08 after hours (aggregator).
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and mix, not price. Q2 2026 net sales ~21 Mbbl/d rising to ~40 Mbo/d on exit as wells came online (35 to 47, heading to 77); Hondo restart adds a lower-sulfur mix. Price is a headwind: sulfur quality deducts and $24-28 per Bbl marketing deducts.
web_suppliers: Midstream and downstream partners are the binding constraint: a 40,000 gross bbl/d sales throughput cap from July 2026, and gas-compressor availability limited online wells as of 2026-06-18. Wireline crews needed for perf adds. No raw-material shortage disclosed. JPMorgan Chase is term-loan agent.
web_customers: Concentrated in unnamed California refineries. In Q2 2026 local refiners displaced imported cargos, then charged sulfur quality deducts and temporarily cut Pacific OCS throughput; Sable is negotiating waterborne sales via Los Angeles marine terminals to widen the buyer set.
web_who_loses: Foreign crude exporters and tanker/cargo sellers displaced from the California market, plus refiners losing import volumes. Also losers: California agencies whose OSFM oversight was replaced by PHMSA under the 2026-08-19 order, and Exxon, repaid and replaced as lender.
web_contradicting_evidence: 2026-08-19 court found Sable violated the consent decree without justification, rejected its force majeure and DPA Section 707 immunity defenses, and ordered $1.449M; California DPA challenge still pending. Added: $18.5M demurrage, sulfur deducts, 40 Mbo/d throughput cap, 15% coupon with 100% excess-cash-flow sweep, $250M ATM ($22.2M used), Jefferies PT cut to $9 on 2026-08-12.
web_if_management_right: All 77 Harmony and Heritage wells online in Q3 2026, Hondo restarts September 2026, 2H26 net sales 40,000-45,000 Boe/d, FY27 42,500-47,500 Boe/d with LOE falling to $9-12 per Boe and capex cut to $85M midpoint; the TLB amortizes and free cash flow funds shareholder returns after the 2027 reserve report.
web_if_management_wrong: Midstream and downstream limits persist at 40 Mbo/d with sulfur deducts and wide differentials, Hondo slips; with a 15% coupon and 100% excess-cash-flow sweep, cash flow misses, forcing more ATM or equity issuance, and P&A financial security obligations revive by 2028-12-22. California litigation could still interrupt operations.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: California refiners and Los Angeles marine terminals getting cheaper Pacific OCS barrels instead of imports; the third-party buyer of the Crimson San Pablo Bay pipeline and San Francisco refinery market; wireline and well-service contractors; JPMorgan underwriting; gas-processing and pipeline vendors.
